growth_problem.classification_rule: growth sd at the 84th percentile of all economies > 75
growth_problem.statement: The growth problem in Armenia is high volatility (growth standard deviation 6.4 over 20 years, above the 75th percentile of all economies). GDP per capita growth over 2016–2025 averaged 5.0 percent a year (2006–2025: 4.9; structural-peer median 2.3), 1.3 standard deviations above the convergence expectation and ranked 1 of 11 among structural peers. GDP per capita is at its peak to date (2025). Since 1991 growth has run in four eras: 1991–2000 at -1.5 percent a year, 2001–2008 at 12.5, 2009–2016 at 1.7 and 2017–2025 at 5.5. Investment (gross fixed capital formation to GDP) is 0.3 standard deviations below expectation given income at 21.1 percent of GDP; the private-public split is unavailable in prototype (IMF Investment and Capital Stock Dataset not ingested). Gross savings is 0.4 standard deviations below expectation given income; the current account balance is -6.2 percent of GDP and net FDI inflows are 1.7 percent of GDP. Structural change (G9) is not computed in the prototype. Exports to GDP is 0.6 standard deviations above expectation given income, and economic complexity is 1.1 standard deviations above expectation (the complexity gap). The relevant question is therefore: what drives the volatility of growth and why investment does not translate into sustained growth. Provisional top-split reading: indeterminate (real lending rate t = 1.7, real private credit growth 8.8 percent, investment t = -0.3).

structural.rule: structural: 10 nearest by Euclidean distance in z-scores of log_gdppc_ppp, log_population, resource_rents (diagonal Mahalanobis), with a landlocked mismatch adding 1 to the squared distance (one sd of a continuous feature); micro-states below 300000 excluded; high-income economies excluded; fragile and conflict-affected economies excluded; candidates with an income observation before 2023 excluded

regional.rule: regional: same region (Europe & Central Asia); income groups within 0 step(s) of Upper middle income until at least 6; capped at 15 nearest by log GDP per capita (PPP)

aspirational.rule: aspirational: GDP per capita (PPP) in 2000 within ±30% of the target's current 20212 and average growth since ≥ 3% a year; up to 10 by growth
